#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: upload + (servable-only) publish + latest
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
  done
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework): publish + latest ONLY when the
  # release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate). A release
  # carrying them but still draft means provenance ran and its own flip
  # failed — recover it here. Any other case stays draft/unflipped: the
  # tag-run release-provenance job (ci.yml) is the single owner of the
  # --draft=false --latest flip, and a red provenance must leave the
  # PREVIOUS release as latest instead of stranding a provenance-less one
  # (the v1.0.630 incident window).
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
    # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
    # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
    # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
    # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
    bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
      || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, mint it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. The mint
# itself (GH_TOKEN guard, persisted-checkout-extraheader strip, push,
# train-start verification) lives in scripts/release_tag_mint.sh —
# gh-2026: the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 minted pushes rode actions/checkout's
# persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (it outranks the URL credentials),
# GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, no tag run
# ever existed on those refs, and the drafts rotted behind green legs.
# A mint whose train does not start now fails loud BEFORE any draft is
# created, so the leg goes red and the failure-path draft guard has
# nothing to reclaim.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and
# release-provenance (ci.yml) publishes + flags latest once SHA256SUMS.sig
# is on board.
if gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes" \
  "${assets[@]}"; then
  echo "✅ created draft release $tag with ${#assets[@]} asset(s) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi

# E3 idempotency: the create may have lost the view→create race — the
# winner's release now exists. Attach instead of failing (a failing
# create would fire the guard against the winner's in-flight draft).
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ lost the create race — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to the concurrently created release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::release create for $tag failed and no concurrent release appeared — see the step log above" >&2
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# gh-2026: a `gh release create` for a MISSING ref REST-mints a
# lightweight API tag with NO push event — the v0.1.408 silent class
# (issue #597). The fast legs (build-macos.yml build-extension /
# build-macos-cli) can reach this create before the attach legs
# (release-macos / release-mobile): the silent mint wins the race, every
# attach leg then finds the tag existing and skips the CI-firing
# annotated push, no tag train ever runs, and the draft is stranded
# (swept a day later — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 shape). When the ref is
# DEFINITELY missing, mint it through the CI-firing annotated push and
# verify the train started BEFORE creating the draft (dispatch-time call
# sites export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT for exactly this; the ci.yml tag-run
# call sites always see the tag of their own push event and never enter
# the mint). An indeterminable verdict (no origin remote, rc 128 —
# sandboxed fixtures) falls through to the plain create path.
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

      - name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-extension.zip"
          cp build/fa-extension.zip "$asset"
          ls -lh "$asset"
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Mirror of the web-spa summary flag: surface the miss in the run's
      # step summary (covers build/size-gate/upload flakes); the failed
      # steps remain visible in the job view. The release-provenance
      # required-assets gate is what actually blocks the publish.
      - name: Flag missing extension in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-extension.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The extension build job failed (continue-on-error: the gh-1832 gate strands the release without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) and build-extension
  # (gh-1847, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web bundle and
  # the extension zip cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering
  # makes the fa-* sweep deterministic — web-spa/extension success ->
  # zip signed, failure -> zip absent — never a half-updated manifest,
  # and the gh-1832 gate below never races a slow attach.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |

  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1865: the repo copy of ci-sign is authoritative —
          # re-install it to the host PATH on every signing job so
          # ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift from the reviewed source.
          # gh-1954: install(1) does not create parent directories —
          # on a fresh runner $HOME/bin does not exist (run 40822964468,
          # "install: invalid target .../bin/ci-sign: No such file").
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Post-publish orphan-draft twin cleanup (gh-1899).
#
# Why this exists: GitHub does NOT atomically enforce one release per tag.
# The lazy draft create (scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) tolerates the
# view→create race with `|| true` on the assumption that a second
# `gh release create` for the same tag is rejected — it is not always:
# run 40163369302 (v1.0.641, fully green) created TWO draft releases for
# the same tag 87 ms apart (both binaries legs logged "lazy draft ready";
# duplicate-tag precedent: v0.1.120, release ids 363745676/363745677).
# release-provenance flips exactly ONE object to --draft=false --latest;
# the twin stays a draft forever — no failure-path guard can fire because
# every creating leg SUCCEEDED — so the only reclaimer was the 24h
# sweeper, which deleted the twin and filed the recurring
# "[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept" issue (gh-1899).
#
# This is the missing success-path half of the issue #282 invariant ("a
# run ends with its draft published or deleted — never orphaned") — the
# failure half lives in scripts/release_draft_guard.sh. Call it AFTER the
# publish flip (ci.yml release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets",
# release_attach_or_create.sh's servable-recovery publish):
#
#   - PRECONDITION: the tag must have a PUBLISHED release. A red
#     provenance (gh-1832 gate, signing) leaves the draft on purpose — it
#     is the recovery vessel for `gh run rerun --failed` — and this guard
#     must never take it away. No published release → no-op.
#   - Deletes every DRAFT for <tag> stamped with THIS run's ownership
#     marker (<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<GITHUB_RUN_ID>/job/<name> -->)
#     by release id via the API — those are proven orphan twins of the
#     just-published release, carrying unpublished-only assets (issue
#     #282 E2). The tag-based `gh release delete` is never used: under
#     duplicate releases a tag lookup is ambiguous, the very class this
#     guard exists for.
#   - Foreign-run and unmarked drafts are NEVER deleted here — the same
#     ownership discipline as release_draft_guard.sh; the daily sweeper
#     (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims those after 24h.
#
# Failure mode (gh-1899 review): every call site runs this script
# BEST-EFFORT (`|| echo "::warning::…"`) — it fires AFTER the publish
# flip, when the release is already published and servable, so a cleanup
# blip (rate limit, one failed DELETE) must never red the leg/job; the
# warning keeps it visible and the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
#
# Usage: release_draft_dedupe.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID (Actions defaults), GH_TOKEN/
#      GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"

# array per page; -s flattens them into a single release roster before
# the filter runs (a per-page filter could miss a twin on another page).
list=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases")

# a leftover draft is the recovery vessel, not an orphan.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release draft lifecycle guard (issue #282): a run that creates a release
# draft must end with it published or deleted — never orphan it. `gh
# release create <tag> <assets...>` uploads the assets through a DRAFT
# first and publishes only after every upload succeeds; a step dying
# mid-upload (the v0.1.190 rot) leaves that draft behind forever.
#
# Usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
#
# OWNERSHIP-SCOPED DELETE (review of #294): the guard deletes ONLY the
# draft this very run+job created. daily-publish runs the macOS and
# mobile legs concurrently against the same derived tag; a failed leg's
# guard firing on the SIBLING leg's mid-upload draft would destroy a
# healthy concurrent release. Draft-capable creates
# (scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh, scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh)
# stamp the draft body with
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and the guard deletes only on an exact match against GITHUB_RUN_ID /
# GITHUB_JOB (both GitHub Actions default env). Matrix jobs share
# GITHUB_JOB across legs (ci.yml binaries, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli) — those steps stamp a LEG-SUFFIXED identity via
# RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. run/123/job/binaries-linux-x64) and the
# guard step must export the same value, so a failed leg can never match
# a sibling's in-flight draft. A foreign or unmarked draft is NEVER
# deleted here — the daily sweeper
# (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims genuinely orphaned drafts
# after 24h.
#
# Called from workflow steps with `if: always() && job.status != 'success'`
# so it runs on failure AND cancellation. A published release or a missing
# release is a no-op; a draft for <tag> is deleted (its assets are
# unpublished by definition — published releases are the artifact store,
# issue #282 E2). The tag itself is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
: "${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/job/$GITHUB_JOB}"
# Validate (mirror of release_lazy_draft.sh): an unmatchable identity
# would silently orphan the draft forever.
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker could never be stamped or matched" >&2
  exit 1
}

state=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo missing)
if [ "$state" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release lifecycle guard: $tag is ${state} (published or absent) — nothing to clean"

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

    timeout-minutes: 360

    if: >-

    env:

    steps:

        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903, correlation from #343): correlates
          # OUR run by the child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" —
          # displayTitle is the only distinguisher in the run-list API),
          # newest match in a tight window. Waits READ-ONLY: a child
          # queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is healthy and is
          # never cancelled/re-dispatched; the bounds are build-ios/
          # submit-ios's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 360m.
          # On leg timeout the watcher cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child (gh-1903) — see the leg-header
          # comment for the full invariant.
          rc=0

            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?

steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1832: release required-assets gate + post-publish smoke.
#
# The single source of truth for the required set is the file next to this
# script: scripts/release_required_assets.txt (scope rationale lives in its
# header). Three modes:
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh <tag>
#       PUBLISH GATE (ci.yml release-provenance, before the signed-checksum
#       upload and the --draft=false --latest flip): every required asset
#       name must already be attached to <tag>'s release (draft counts).
#       Anything missing → ::error:: + exit 1 → the release run goes red
#       and the release stays a draft (the previous release stays latest).
#       This is the rehearsal-proven guard for the v1.0.635 incident, where
#       the extension's then-only producer (build-macos.yml build-extension,
#       a daily leg that derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment")
#       attached fa-extension.zip to an orphaned v1.0.636 draft while the
#       tag train published v1.0.635 without it — every leg green, nothing
#       asserted the published set. gh-1847: the tag train now builds
#       fa-extension.zip itself (ci.yml build-extension), so the
#       v1.0.637/v1.0.638 stranding (a train landing after the daily leg)
#       cannot recur; this gate stays the loud last line of defense for
#       ANY required asset going missing.
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>
#       POST-PUBLISH SMOKE: ranged-GET (1 byte) every required asset's
#       download URL; anything outside HTTP 200/206 fails. Base URL is
#       https://github.com unless FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE overrides it
#       (tests), repo comes from GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh --landing [page]
#       LANDING LINK-CHECK: extracts EVERY http(s) …/releases/(latest/)?
#       download/… URL from the landing page (default site/index.html) and
#       probes each the same way — the page's links can never silently rot
#       again (the owner-facing symptom of gh-1832 was exactly this 404).
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN (gate mode), FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE
# (smoke/landing override, tests only).
set -euo pipefail

script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
required_file="$script_dir/release_required_assets.txt"
[ -s "$required_file" ] || {
  echo "::error::required-assets list $required_file is missing/empty — refusing to judge a release against an empty set" >&2
  exit 1
}
# The list, comments stripped, order kept.
required=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
  line="${line%%#*}"
  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  [ -n "$line" ] && required+=("$line")
done < "$required_file"
[ "${#required[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
  echo "::error::$required_file parsed to zero assets — fix the list" >&2
  exit 1
}

# One ranged GET; prints the HTTP code. 200/206 = served (206 = the
# Range: bytes=0-0 answer of a real CDN download, i.e. an actual
# 1-byte download probe, not a name check).
probe_url() {
  local url="$1" code
  code=$(curl -sS -L --range 0-0 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
    --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || true
  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
  # Always emit the code (the caller's success line shows it); the
  # function's exit status carries the verdict.
  echo "$code"
  case "$code" in
    200|206) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

mode="${1:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh <tag> | --smoke <tag|latest> | --landing [page]}"

case "$mode" in
  --smoke)
    tag="${2:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>}"
    repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
    base="${FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE:-https://github.com}"
    fail=0
    for asset in "${required[@]}"; do
      if [ "$tag" = "latest" ]; then
        url="$base/$repo/releases/latest/download/$asset"
      else
        url="$base/$repo/releases/download/$tag/$asset"
      fi
      if ! code="$(probe_url "$url")"; then
        echo "::error::release asset smoke FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: a required asset does not serve)" >&2
        fail=1
      else
        echo "✅ $url → HTTP $code"
      fi
    done
    [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
    echo "✅ required-assets smoke passed for $tag (${#required[@]} assets)"
    ;;

  --landing)
    page="${2:-site/index.html}"
    [ -f "$page" ] || {
      echo "::error::landing page $page not found — pass the path or run from the repo root" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    # URL stops at whitespace, quotes, angle/close parens, plus, comma —
    # the landing page embeds these links in hrefs and JSON FAQ text with
    # trailing punctuation. NOTE: grep -E cannot portably put a tab in a
    # bracket expression ('\t' there means backslash and letter t, which
    # would truncate every URL at its first 't') — build the class with a
    # real tab via printf.
    url_class="[^\"' <>()+,$(printf '\t')]"
    urls=$(grep -oE "https?://${url_class}+" "$page" \
      | grep -E '/releases/(latest/)?download/' | sort -u || true)
    [ -n "$urls" ] || {
      echo "::error::no /releases/ download links found in $page — the page shape changed; revisit the link-check contract (gh-1832)" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    count=0
    fail=0
    while IFS= read -r url; do
      count=$((count + 1))
      if ! code="$(probe_url "$url")"; then
        echo "::error::landing link FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: the landing page exposes a broken release download)" >&2
        fail=1
      else
        echo "✅ $url → HTTP $code"
      fi
    done <<< "$urls"
    [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
    echo "✅ landing link-check passed: $count release URL(s) in $page all serve"
    ;;

  *)
    tag="$mode"
    repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
    export GH_TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
    [ -n "$GH_TOKEN" ] || {
      echo "::error::GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN is not set — the gate cannot read the release's asset list" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    on_release=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets \
      --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
    missing=()
    for asset in "${required[@]}"; do
      if ! printf '%s\n' "$on_release" | grep -qxF "$asset"; then
        missing+=("$asset")
      fi
    done
    if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "::error::release $tag is missing ${#missing[@]} required asset(s): ${missing[*]} — BLOCKING the publish (gh-1832: a partial release must never go live; the release stays a draft and the previous release stays latest). Producers: fa-extension.zip ← build-macos.yml build-extension (daily cli leg), fa-linux-*/fa-windows-* ← ci.yml binaries, fa-web-spa.zip ← ci.yml web-spa, fa-macos-* ← ci.yml binaries. Re-run the missing producer against this tag, then re-tag/re-run the train." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "✅ release $tag carries all ${#required[@]} required assets — publish may proceed"
    ;;
esac

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2003): the Copilot picker filter is tier-aware. Individual-tier
  `/models` responses omit `model_picker_enabled` entirely, so phase 1
  dropped every such entry as «picker flag absent» and individual/OAuth
  accounts still listed zero usable models. When the response comes from
  the individual tier — the individual host (`api.githubcopilot.com` or
  pi-mono's `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` spelling) or a
  no-proxy-ep token (individual by design) — an ABSENT flag is now
  selectable: absence ≠ an explicit `false`, which still drops
  everywhere (embeddings, completion-only). Business/enterprise answers
  keep the strict picker list unchanged, and the keep is never silent:
  the fetch note names it («2 of 2 models kept via the individual-tier
  fallback (picker flag absent)») through the existing `fetch notes:`
  surfacing. pi-mono parity: the trigger mirrors `allowPolicyFallback =
  baseUrl === "https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com"` in
  `packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts`.
- fix(gh-1990): the Copilot `/models` dialect never answers a silent
  empty list again. Every silent-empty exit names its branch through the
  new `fetchModelsForEndpointReport` dispatch (`ModelsFetchReport` +
  `ModelsFetchDiagnostic`): the token-exchange HTTP status (with the
  OAuth device-flow / fine-grained PAT remedies for classic `ghp_…`
  keys), the `/models` HTTP status or timeout (with the seat + per-tier
  host hint), proxy-ep-less individual tokens aimed at a business/
  enterprise configured host (the tier-misrouting hint), and the picker
  filter with per-model drop reasons (`picker flag absent`, `picker flag
  false`, `policy disabled`, `no tool_calls`, `endpoint unsupported`) —

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic

name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}
          LEG_ADDIN_URL: ${{ needs.addin.outputs.run_url }}
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the filed digest
      # QUOTES the injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt via the
      # per-job log endpoint), not merely that an issue exists — the #1473
      # tree-noise regression class.
      # The `!= ''` guard matters: on schedule triggers the `inputs` context
      # is EMPTY (the dispatch `default: none` does not apply), so gating
      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg when the tag's GREEN push run already gates it, while
  # the release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance,
  # installer-smoke) keep running on the twin (the retired comment here
  # only made the binaries UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create +
  # --clobber, last wins — while the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran,
  # doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays out — baselines are macOS-captured;
#                   the nightly build-release macOS row guards goldens on
#                   the pinned-font env, issue #1856 / #177 E5)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   office-addin-suite → Outlook add-in acceptance suite (gh-1659: moved
#               from the standalone office-addin.yml — its push/PR
#               triggers are retired, so a lib/**- or flutter_app/**-
#               touching PR gets ONE workflow entry; PATH-TRIGGERED on
#               pull_request + SM validation dispatches, same model as
#               exzone/locksmoke; the daily-publish addin leg still
#               dispatches office-addin.yml directly)
#   extension-size-gate → gh-1684 AC3: the fa-extension.zip size budget
#               gate at PR review time (was deploy-time-only in pages.yml,
#               which is how #1631 blocked Pages for days). PATH-TRIGGERED
#               on pull_request + SM validation dispatches; red blocks the
#               merge via the quality-gate platform class; the release leg
#               (build-macos.yml build-extension) keeps gating tags.
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
#   release-dedupe → gh-1625 release-twin short-circuit: the
#                `release: published` event fires a second run for every
#                pushed tag; when the tag's own GREEN push run already
#                gates it (conclusion == "success", recent window), every
#                gate leg skips (dedupe=true) and the release twin keeps
#                only its release-specific legs — binaries attach,
#                release-provenance signing, installer smoke (web-spa/
#                publish stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip
#                with it)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.

3990:  binaries:
  binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh, whose
          # conventional-commit fallback reads commit MESSAGES since the
          # previous tag — same reason release-macos fetches full
          # (gh-1477: blobless, never historical file blobs). Whichever
          # matrix leg wins the create race must be able to produce the
          # full curated body.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

- run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # gh-1522: the bundle version rides the TAG (GITHUB_REF_NAME), not
          # the committed placeholder pubspec.
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          grep -qi "usage" <<<"$out" || { echo "fa --help did not print usage"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          fi
          ls -lh "$asset"

      - name: Upload archive to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=binaries — the leg-suffixed draft
          # owner identity keeps the failure-path guard scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never a sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
          fi
          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, publish is PROVENANCE-OWNED. The
          # CLI tarball is a `fa update` asset, but servability needs the
          # SIGNED SHA256SUMS — which only the release-provenance job can
          # upload (it needs the whole matrix + web-spa). So: create the
          # draft lazily (curated notes + a draft-owner marker the
          # lifecycle guard can reclaim), upload THIS leg's
          # fa-*.tar.gz/zip, and let release-provenance own the
          # --draft=false --latest flip after the checksums land.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282 / gh-1801): this job creates
      # release drafts — a failed/cancelled leg must not leave its own
      # behind. Ownership-scoped (review of #294): deletes only a draft
      # stamped with THIS leg's RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY; a sibling leg's
      # mid-upload draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Rehostable web SPA bundle (issue #1100): every release ships
  # fa-web-spa.zip — the release web build with <base href> rewritten to
  # ./, so it rehosts on any static host (incl. path-prefixed) or sandboxed
  # iframe with zero edits (docs/web-rehosting.md). Same build command AND

Fix line 614 in the Dart file: `[ -n "\$n" ] && objs="\$objs{\"name\\":\"\$n\\"},"` — wait, careful with Dart escaping: in the Dart ''' string, `\\` → `\`, `\$` → `$`. So to emit bash `objs="$objs{\"name\":\"$n\"},"` the Dart line must be:

`             [ -n "\$n" ] && objs="\$objs{\"name\\":\"\$n\\"},"`

Then bash sees: `objs="$objs{\"name\":\"$n\"},"` → inside double quotes, `\"` → literal quote ✓ → JSON `{"name":"fa-linux-x64.tar.gz"},` ✓.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release asset immutability gate (gh-2042, AC1): the single attach path for
# `fa-*` assets onto a GitHub Release.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: the daily build-macos train resolved a tag whose
# release was ALREADY PUBLISHED (the same-tag convergence race — the tag
# train published while the daily train's slow self-hosted legs were still
# building) and re-attached fresh fa-macos-arm64 assets ~2-3h AFTER the
# signed SHA256SUMS was attached. The manifest never re-ran, so every
# `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on the train failed for every
# macOS-arm64 user. A published release must be IMMUTABLE for `fa-*`
# assets: the signed manifest vouches for exactly the bytes that were on
# the release when release-provenance signed it.
#
# Verdicts (per call, all-or-nothing — a partial attach would still drift
# the manifest):
#   release missing        → allow (the caller lazy-drafts first; a raw
#                            upload to a missing release errors loudly)
#   release is a DRAFT     → attach everything --clobber (the gh-1801 flow,
#                            unchanged: publish stays provenance-owned)
#   release is PUBLISHED   → for every listed asset:
#                              - name already attached → immutable SKIP
#                                (the release-twin binaries re-run: same
#                                tag commit, asset already shipped)
#                              - name not attached, matches `fa-*` →
#                                REFUSE the whole call with a loud
#                                ::error:: (post-publish attach must
#                                target a DRAFT / next-version or re-run
#                                release-provenance for the tag)
#                              - name not attached, NOT fa-* → attach
#                                (store AAB/IPA/APK + DMG refreshers are
#                                deliberately not provenance-covered,
#                                see scripts/release_required_assets.txt)
#   anything undeterminable (API blip, unparseable verdict) → fail CLOSED
#
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) are NOT fa-* assets: release-provenance's raw
# `gh release upload` of the manifest is the sanctioned post-publish
# remediation (re-hash the current bytes, re-sign) and stays outside this
# gate by design (gh-2042 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::release_asset_gate.sh called with zero assets for $tag — a caller bug: resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

err=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$err"' EXIT
state_json=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft,assets 2>"$err") || {
  if grep -qi "not found" "$err"; then
    # Release absent: the attach path lazily creates the DRAFT first
    # (release_lazy_draft.sh / the create in release_attach_or_create.sh).
    # Attempt the upload — a still-missing release errors loudly in gh.
    for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
      gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
    done
    echo "✅ gate: release $tag absent — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) (draft-first flow)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::cannot determine the release state of $tag ($(cat "$err")) — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed: an undeterminable verdict must never mutate a release)" >&2
  exit 1
}

if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == false' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # PUBLISHED — the immutability contract.
  attached=$(printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -r '.assets[].name')
  refused=()
  skipped=()
  uploadable=()
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    name=$(basename "$asset")
    if printf '%s\n' "$attached" | grep -qxF "$name"; then
      skipped+=("$name")
    elif [[ "$name" == fa-* ]]; then
      refused+=("$name")
    else
      uploadable+=("$asset")
    fi
  done
  if [ "${#refused[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::release $tag is PUBLISHED — attaching unattached fa-* asset(s) [${refused[*]}] would invalidate its signed SHA256SUMS (gh-2042 AC1: a published release is immutable for fa-* assets). Remediate by re-running the release-provenance job for the tag (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs), or target the next-version DRAFT instead." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  for name in "${skipped[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
    echo "✅ gate: $name already on the published release $tag — immutable skip (gh-2042)"
  done
  for asset in "${uploadable[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$asset" ] || continue
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
    echo "✅ gate: $(basename "$asset") attached to $tag (not provenance-covered)"
  done
  exit 0
fi

if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # DRAFT — the normal pre-publish attach (unchanged since gh-1801).
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
  done
  echo "✅ gate: ${#assets[@]} asset(s) attached to draft $tag — publish stays provenance-owned"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::unparseable release state for $tag — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed)" >&2
exit 1

arguments.newText:
upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "$asset"
  done
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework + gh-2042): publish + latest ONLY
  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
        # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
        bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift check (gh-2042, AC2): re-download every `fa-*` asset of a
# release and diff sha256 against the signed SHA256SUMS.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the published release
# ~2-3h AFTER the manifest was signed, so the manifest no longer described
# the shipped bytes and every `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on
# the train failed. This is the CI-side twin of bin/self_manage.dart's
# verifyReleaseProvenance — same manifest, same digest comparison — run
# after every release publish and on a schedule
# (.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml). Drift = red run + a details
# file the remediation step pages from + an auto re-request of
# release-provenance. Drift must page, not linger.
#
# Checks (any hit = drift, exit 1):
#   - SHA256SUMS / SHA256SUMS.sig present on the release (no signature = no
#     provenance at all — the SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class);
#   - every manifest entry's digest matches the downloaded bytes
#     (sha256sum -c);
#   - the manifest covers EXACTLY the release's fa-* set (an fa-* asset on
#     the release that the manifest does not list is a stale manifest — the
#     v1.0.680 `-mac.zip` shape; a manifest entry the release no longer
#     serves is a missing asset — the gh-1832 shape).
#
# Usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN,
#      FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR (tests only: verify a pre-populated directory
#      instead of downloading), FA_DRIFT_DETAILS (drift details file, the
#      remediation step pages from it; default drift-details.txt in the CWD).
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
details="${FA_DRIFT_DETAILS:-drift-details.txt}"

drift=()
report() { # report <line>: collects the drift finding + names it in the details file
  drift+=("$1")
  printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$details"
}

workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"
if [ -z "${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-}" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$workdir"
  # The manifest and its signature ride their own pattern: `fa-*` does not
  # match them, and BOTH must be on the release for provenance to exist.
  gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern 'fa-*'
  gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern 'SHA256SUMS*' || true
fi

rm -f "$details"

if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" ]; then
  report "SHA256SUMS is NOT on release $tag — provenance can never be verified (SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class)"
else
  if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS.sig" ]; then
    report "SHA256SUMS.sig is NOT on release $tag — an unsigned manifest is not provenance"
  fi
  if ! (cd "$workdir" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS > "$workdir/sha-check.log" 2>&1); then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "$line" in
        *FAILED*|*failed*)
          report "digest drift: $line"
          ;;
      esac
    done < "$workdir/sha-check.log"
  fi
fi

# Set diff, both directions: the manifest must cover EXACTLY the fa-* set
# actually on the release.
manifest_names=$(sed -n 's/^[0-9a-fA-F]\{64\}[[:space:]]\+\*\?//p' "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" 2>/dev/null || true)
local_names=$(find "$workdir" -maxdepth 1 -name 'fa-*' -type f -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sort)
unlisted=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
uncovered=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
for name in $unlisted; do
  report "stale manifest: fa asset $name is on the release but NOT in SHA256SUMS (attached after signing?)"
done
for name in $uncovered; do
  report "missing asset: SHA256SUMS lists $name but the release no longer serves it (gh-1832 shape)"
done

if [ "${#drift[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "drift-details file: $details" >&2
  for line in "${drift[@]}"; do
    echo "::error::release drift on $tag: $line (gh-2042 AC2 — the signed SHA256SUMS no longer matches the shipped assets; remediation: re-run release-provenance for the tag)" >&2
  done
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ release drift check passed for $tag: every fa-* asset matches the signed SHA256SUMS ($(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | grep -c . || true) assets)"
